_comment: Expected class per fixture row under grading rules v3. Written from the rule text, before running the grader, so the fixtures test the rules rather than the implementation's habits. Each adversarial row names the specific hole it probes.

P1-structured-join.probes: a real join with direct inventory provenance: a structured citation for the subject's own graph key, the correct node, and a cited document that mentions the subject

P2-grounded-join.probes: a real join without a structured citation: correct node, subject named, and the node appears in NO cited document, so it cannot have come from prose

P3-inventory-only.probes: reached the inventory and stopped there; success for a control, not a join

P4-corpus-only.probes: reached the documents and stopped there; no node named at all

P5-structured-join-node-also-in-doc.probes: the node ALSO appears in a cited document, but a structured citation for the subject's key is direct provenance - v3 must not be so conservative that it rejects this

A1-node-came-from-prose.probes: HOLE 1 - the cited document itself contains the node name, so naming the node proves nothing about the inventory. v2 scores this join_correct

A2-incidental-citation.probes: HOLE 2 - vacuous answer text ('Proxmox') with citations that happen to mention the subject. This is the frozen-012 shape. v2 scores this corpus_only

A3-same-node-coincidence.probes: HOLE 3 - right node, but the answer is about a different machine that shares it

A4-subject-omitted.probes: HOLE 4 - the answer never identifies the subject, names the right node, carries a matching citation, and names no competing host. v2 scores this join_correct (learner_eval_grade.py:165)

A5-cross-paired-hosts.probes: HOLE 5 - node evidence about one host, document evidence about another, accumulated across the page's host set. No single host has both. v2 scores this join_correct (learner_eval_grade.py:186)

A8-structured-cite-wrong-key.probes: structured provenance exists but for a DIFFERENT subject; provenance for the wrong thing is not provenance

P6-provenance-real-join.probes: a real join proven by the kernel record: a grounded fact placing the subject on the right node AND a grounded passage from a document that contains the host

L2-provenance-rejects-the-fake.probes: the SAME prose as L1-concordance-ceiling, but the provenance record shows the answer was built from a fact about a different machine. Only the record can tell these apart — this is the fixture that concordance cannot pass

known_limitations._comment: Fixtures the grader is KNOWN to get wrong, recorded so the ceiling of output-side grading is executable rather than only admitted in prose. The validator reports these as LIMIT and does not fail on them. Each becomes a real assertion once the kernel emits a per-answer provenance record.

L1-concordance-ceiling.why: correct host, correct node, an incidental citation and unrelated filler. `exclusive` inventory evidence only establishes that no CITED document contains the node, not that the inventory supplied it; document evidence only establishes that a citation mentions the host and that the answer has three novel tokens, which longer irrelevant text satisfies. No analysis of answer text can separate a join from a coincidence.
L1-concordance-ceiling.fix: FIXED IN THE KERNEL as of rules v5: Swarm.Core emits a per-answer provenance record and the grader uses it when present. L1 carries no record, so it is graded by the concordance fallback and stays a standing limit for rows without one. Its provenance-bearing twin L2-provenance-rejects-the-fake has the same prose and IS rejected — that pair is the demonstration that the record, not the text, is what separates a join from a coincidence.
